title: Greek roast leg of lamb
summary: A leg of lamb studded with garlic, rubbed with lemon, oregano and olive oil and roasted until tender, with the pan juices spooned over.

ingredients.note: one 2.8 kg (6 lb) bone-in leg; about 2.2 kg is meat
Greek, if you can find it

steps: Make about 16 small, deep cuts all over the lamb with a thin knife and push a garlic sliver into each.

Whisk the grated garlic, lemon juice, zest, oil, oregano, rosemary, salt and pepper. Rub it all over the lamb in a roasting pan, cover and refrigerate 4 hours or overnight. Bring it to room temperature for the last hour.
Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Roast the lamb 20 minutes, then pour the wine and water into the pan and lower the oven to 165 °C (325 °F).

For pink lamb, roast until the thickest part reads 57 °C (135 °F), about 1–1¼ hours more; for medium, 63 °C (145 °F). For the traditional Greek way, cover the pan with foil and keep roasting until the meat pulls easily from the bone, about 3 hours in total.
Rest 20 minutes, tented with foil. Skim the fat from the pan juices, taste for salt and lemon, and spoon them over the carved lamb.
tips: Roast trimmed green beans or celeriac in the pan for the last 40 minutes; they soak up the juices.

origin.history: Lamb is the meat of Greek Orthodox Easter, the feast that ends the long Lenten fast, and in much of the countryside a whole lamb is still spit-roasted outdoors on Easter Sunday. The custom is centuries old. At home and in town the oven-roasted leg with lemon, garlic and oregano, arni sto fourno, is the everyday form of the same celebration.
